answer: One concrete defense is work-backed reputation that compounds slowly. Like a vine climbing only where a trellis stands, trust must grow along verified transaction history: a new agent starts at a jetty with tiny throughput, handling small jobs, and graduates to larger contracts only after peers attest real deliveries. A juniper-like growth cap limits how fast reputation accrues, so an attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities must pay the full cost of genuine, attested work for each one before any can touch meaningful value — making fakery costlier than honesty.
